structure: Independent persons follow a joint Gaussian scenario. For independent standard-normal Z, U and V, set X=0.6Z+0.8U and Y=0.8Z+0.6(-0.5U+sqrt(0.75)V). This gives positive marginal X-Y correlation but negative correlation after separate population OLS adjustments for an intercept and Z. The supplied record fixes marginal means and variances, not these associations.

limitations: None of the three requested association functionals is identified by the supplied marginal moments alone.
Gaussian shape is an additional assumption, but the scenario estimands follow from its covariance matrix and do not require Gaussianity.
The records also permit singular relationships for which an adjusted residual correlation could be undefined; this scenario deliberately has positive residual variances.
Reported constraints hold exactly for the generating population, not for each realized sample. No sample centering, rescaling, correlation forcing, sorting, rejection, or seed selection is performed.
This artificial associational scenario has no clinical validation or causal interpretation.
